contentSummary: This is the thinnest page in the green-recycling cluster: a fixed-height banner followed by a single navy-to-teal gradient card holding one intro paragraph and one nine-item bulleted list. The paragraph frames end-of-life ship dismantling as a hazard problem, naming asbestos, PCBs, glass fibre, solid foam and waste oil as the on-board materials that threaten environment and human health. The list is the actual substance — a chain-of-custody procedure running from the ship owner handing over the IHM before purchase, through labelling, plan-driven handling, trained removal under HSE supervision, dedicated temporary yard storage, authorised sub-contractor collection against a manifest, and HSE…
